name: Glasses to mask facial flaws

lead: Thick or oversized frames are worn to pull attention away from features people dislike, such as under-eye bags, asymmetry or the nose.

Frames add visual weight around the eyes and nose bridge, which proponents say redirects the viewer's attention to the eyewear. Glasses are now widely worn as fashion accessories, including non-prescription pairs.

paras: People pick bold acetate or oversized frames, sometimes non-prescription, and wear them daily or for photos. The effect is visible as soon as they are on.
No health risks. Results depend on the person, and heavy frames can feel uncomfortable on the nose or ears.

chain: Eye bags, asymmetry or nose less prominent
angle.text: Chunky or oversized frames add visual weight around the eyes, drawing attention away from bags, asymmetry or the nose. The frames are visibly present and change what stands out on the face.

lead: Glasses to mask facial flaws is a style practice of wearing thick or large frames to draw attention from features a person dislikes, such as eye bags, asymmetry or the nose. Wikipedia describes glasses as now widely worn as fashion accessories, including non-prescription pairs.[1]
No studies were found testing whether frames conceal or change the perception of facial features.

paras: Frames come in many styles and materials, and many consumers buy non-prescription glasses as accessories.[1] Appearance communities discuss thick frames as a way to cover under-eye bags or distract from asymmetry; no community sources were available to quote.
